title: Interactive kernel probing and slab defragmentation guided by decode signal
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: On high-concurrency serving hosts we observe that KV slab fragmentation increases decode tail latency and causes suboptimal kernel choices for short prefix-heavy requests. Existing eviction heuristics are reactive and treat kernel selection as independent from allocation state, which leads to repeated decode stalls when the runtime switches kernels mid-decode or when fragmented slabs force small-copies.

Goal: Implement an interactive probing and coordination mechanism where the decode path emits lightweight signals about upcoming decode shapes (active token windows, affinity hints) that drive two cooperative subsystems: (1) a kernel-probing module that measures candidate kernel latency/throughput under current slab residency and selects the best kernel for the immediate decode wave, and (2) a slab defragmentation controller that opportunistically coalesces neighboring fragments when decode signal indicates stable multi-token growth. The approach should reduce p95/p99 tail regressions at the cluster-level and avoid kernel churn during in-flight decodes.

Design overview:
- Decode-signal payload: 4-byte tag emitted at prefill completion and updated at decode boundaries indicating expected forward-span, tenancy (tenant id hash), and affinity hint (e.g., prefer-fused-attn). This is intentionally small to avoid scheduling overhead.
- Kernel-probing module: maintains a per-shard lightweight history of microbenchmarks (windowed median over last N waves) keyed by (sequence-band, quantization-mode, slab-occupancy-class). Probing executed inline for cold kernels with a budgeted micro-benchmark (<=100us) to estimate candidate latency. The module exposes a fast decision API used by the scheduler to pick the kernel before the first token.
- Defragmentation controller: a background coalescer that performs local slab-copy compactions only when decode signals predict an upcoming stable multi-token decode and GPU free cycles are available. Uses a soft-credit admission so it never evicts or migrates pages required by in-flight decodes.
- Coordination policy: kernel-probing and defragmentation are coupled via a short-lived lease token. If probing indicates the 'compact-friendly' kernel is superior and decode signal predicts growth > horizon, controller attempts compact; otherwise scheduler selects a kernel that favors latency even if suboptimal cost.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end p50 improvement >= 2% and p95 improvement >= 8% on tenant workloads with high short-sequence churn (internal benchmark).
- Reduction in kernel switches during single decode > 50% compared to baseline.
- No increase in OOMs or end-to-end error rate.
- CPU/GPU overhead for probing + defrag <= 3% of host cycles on average.
comments: 2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Initial ticket created after spike tracing showed repeated kernel swaps during 8-16 token bursts. Linked to slab fragmentation on hosts with mixed tenant thermal patterns.

2026-03-11 Aisha Patel: Design review notes: prefer minimal signal size; avoid cross-tenant compaction unless soft-isolation credit allows. Suggest per-shard probe history with decay factor 0.7. Also request experiment harness for probe budget tuning.

2026-03-12 Priya Singh (perf): Ran microbench harness on p4d-sim nodes. Baseline median single-token kernel latency 0.42ms, fused kernel 0.36ms when slab compacted. Observed compact cost ~0.9ms for 2 pages. Suggest budget probe cap 80us and compact threshold 3 contiguous fragments.

2026-03-13 Aisha Patel: Implementation plan sketched. Work items: 1) add decode-signal field to prefill acknowledgement (proto delta), 2) implement probe history cache with eviction TTL 15s, 3) defrag controller with soft-credit queue per shard, 4) metrics & alerts: kernel_switches_per_decode, avg_probe_latency, compaction_time_ms. Created feature branch runtime/eng/274512-slab-probe.

2026-03-14 Marco Ruiz: Early integration test against the canary pool. Observed kernel switches reduced by ~62% for synthetic short-burst workload; p95 token latency down 9.3% on canary. Noted edge case: when host GPU is saturated compaction backpressure increases queue latency by ~1.2ms. Next: add adaptive backoff and limit compaction concurrency to 1 per GPU.

2026-03-14 QA: Added unit tests for probe-history TTL and a stress test that simulates alternating tenant bursts. Found race where lease token not released if compaction fails; patch required. Filed sub-issue ENG-274513 to track compaction error handling.

2026-03-14 Aisha Patel: Flagging rollout plan: first enable kernel-probing in read-only mode (metrics only) for 48h, then enable soft compaction on hosts with > 40% free VRAM and < 70% GPU utilization. Rollout toggles controlled by runtime feature flag slab.compact.experimental.

2026-03-14 Marco Ruiz: Dependencies: requires small protobuf change stored in repo infra/proto/prefill.proto (PR link below), a canary Grafana dashboard, and updated kernel selection unit tests. Estimate still 8 points.

2026-03-14 Engineering: Linked artifacts: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482, benchmark dashboard https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/bsd123/paged-attn-probe-canary, spike notes https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xk_probe_spike

2026-03-14 Next steps: finish compaction backoff, fix lease-release race, increase unit test coverage, run 72h canary, collect perf and error budget metrics, prepare runbook for rollback if compaction-induced stalls detected.
